newsitem.title: USA: Florida tobacco cases go forward despite accord.
newsitem.headline: Florida tobacco cases go forward despite accord.

text.p: Two of the tobacco cases being heard in Florida courts went ahead on Monday in spite of a sweeping accord between state attorneys general and cigarette makers announced on Friday.

In Miami, attorneys resumed the slow process of jury selection in Norma Broin vs. Philip Morris Cos Inc, a $5 billion class-action lawsuit filed on behalf of thousands of flight attendants allegedly sickened by breathing secondhand smoke on U.S.-based passenger jets.

By Monday, the 13th day of jury selection, attorneys had selected 75 members of the pool from which a panel of six jurors and an estimated 10 alternates will be chosen. Eventually, 100 people are expected to be in the pool.

In West Palm Beach, a pre-trial hearing went ahead in Florida's lawsuit seeking to recoup $1.1 billion or more in Medicaid funds spent on treatment for sick smokers. A trial is scheduled to begin August 4.

In a contentious session before Florida Circuit Court Judge Harold Cohen, Brown & Williamson Tobacco Corp attorney David Berneck cited numerous still-secret documents that allegedly showed lawyers did not influence the results of any scientific investigation by tobacco companies into the hazards of smoking. Brown & Williamson is a unit of B.A.T Industries Plc.
W.C. Gentry, an attorney representing the state of Florida, accused Burneck of pulling tobacco company documents out of context.

"This is totally improper," he said during the first of eight days of testimony in which tobacco companies will seek to dismiss Florida's suit, saying the state has insufficient evidence to support the allegations in its complaint.
An emergency hearing was scheduled later Monday in Engle vs. R.J. Reynolds, another class-action suit filed by Stanley and Susan Rosenblatt, who filed the Broin case.
Stanley Rosenblatt said he would present a motion at the hearing that Dade County Circuit Judge Alan Postman declare that the settlement would not affect the Engle case.
